items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: our pianist, his name was Jerome Carrington... it would buy food for all of us to eat

ctx.x: -- and what'd you -- take up residence then in Chicago?

Yes, we -- we worked outside -- some one got us an apartment there it was a very fine lady and she put the whole band up out on the South Side, out on the South Side, and we stayed in this apartment, we had no money and our pianist, his name was Jerome Carrington, he was -- he -- he got a job with Charlie Cook, and when he would get his money

he would give (his Family) it -- gladly) a little money and it would buy food for all of us to eat. And we did that for quite a long time. And I was quite -- I guess the last one to get a gig when I was there because I was playing saxophone and cornet at that time.
